$description: Colour: the neutral ramp, the roles built on it, the action colour, the states, diff and code colours, and the marks. One declaration per colour, holding both schemes.

neutral-0.$description:
── Neutral ramp ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Twelve steps, up from five. The gap that mattered most: there was no
hover or pressed background token, so every interactive surface in
both repos was improvising.

Deliberately COOL — a cool grey lets the warm mark and the amber
attention state read as warm, instead of muddying into them.

ONE TEMPERATURE, top to bottom, both themes: every tinted step sits at
OKLCH hue 286° (±3°, `npm run check` holds it). Chroma is a whisper at
the ends (~0.0015 at neutral-25) and peaks in the mid-tones (~0.015 at
neutral-700), where a grey reads most neutral-flat without it. Only pure
white (light neutral-0) is untinted. An earlier ramp mixed warm hairlines
(106°) with cool text, so a border and the label beside it disagreed.

Changing a step: keep its OKLCH lightness, keep the hue, re-run the
check.

bg.$description:
Semantic aliases. Components use THESE, not the raw steps.
Where a role sits on a different step in each theme, the step's two
hexes are written out (rule 2) and named in the comment; the check
holds them to the ramp.

surface-sticky.$description:
Sticky chrome — a header or toolbar that content scrolls under, usually
with `backdrop-filter: blur()`. 92% of the surface it sits on: the card
in light, the page ground in dark, where cards are lighter than the
page. A token so consumers never color-mix() one (DESIGN.md §11).

io.brignano.note: neutral-600 / neutral-500 — text-safe: eyebrows, axis labels, captions

line-control.$description:
The edge that tells you a control is there: inputs, secondary buttons.
WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of a boundary you need to find the control, which
--line-strong is nowhere near. Light is neutral-500 (3.44:1 on card, 3.29:1
on bg); dark sits between neutral-400 and neutral-500, which the ramp has no step
for (3.39:1 on card, 3.68:1 on bg).

device.$description:
A phone's bezel (.pp-device). A phone is a dark object in either theme,
so this stays dark rather than flipping with --ink, which would draw a
near-white bezel in dark mode. Dark lifts it to neutral-300 so the frame still
has an edge against the near-black page. Decoration, not a boundary.

action.$description:
── Interactive — cobalt ─────────────────────────────────────────────
Everything you can act on: links, buttons, focus, selection. Chosen to
be semantically INERT — it carries no inherited meaning the way amber,
green and red do — and complementary to the mark hue, so identity and
affordance never compete for the same attention.

Every step sits at OKLCH hue 256° (`npm run check` holds it), as near
to larch's opposite (~248°) as sRGB allows while keeping cobalt's
chroma. It is deliberately NOT Tailwind's blue-600 (263°, a touch
violet and electric): same affordance, our own colour (ADR-0008).

  --action          fill               5.18:1 / 3.78:1  (label 5.18 / 4.73)
  --action-ink      link/icon/focus    6.78:1 / 7.07:1
  --action-hover    hover fill         label 8.65:1 / 5.88:1
  --action-ink-hover  hovered link     8.65:1 / 9.95:1 on --card
  --action-pressed  pressed fill       label 10.44:1 / 7.52:1

The fill is a saturated mid-cobalt with a WHITE label in both themes,
and hover and pressed step darker in both. Dark used to lift the fill
to the ink's pale blue with a dark label, which read as washed out on
the most important control on the screen. So in dark the fill and the
ink are now different steps: --action fills, --action-ink is what you read
(links, icons, the focus ring). The dark fill is as light as a white
label allows (4.5:1), which is what keeps it 3:1 as a mark on --card,
--bg and its own wash.

DISABLED IS NEUTRAL, NEVER HUED — a greyed-out control must stop
signalling "click me".

action-ink-hover.$description:
A hovered link is TEXT, so it follows the ink, not the fill: in dark the
fill's hover is too deep to read on a dark page (about 3.3:1).

danger-fill.$description:
A button filled with danger (.btn-danger), and its label. Its own
tokens so the state hue --danger can stay a pale, readable rust in dark
(messages, pills, field errors) while the button is as deep as the
primary beside it: as light as a white label allows, stepping darker on
hover and press (ADR-0015). In light the fills ARE --danger and
--danger-ink; `npm run check` holds them to those.

  --danger-fill          label 6.10:1 / 4.58:1   on --card 3.91:1 in dark
  --danger-fill-hover    label 7.92:1 / 5.65:1
  --danger-fill-pressed  label 7.92:1 / 6.96:1

success.$description:
── State ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Three hues, one meaning each, identical on every surface and both
tiers. Always shipped with an ICON AND A WORD — colour is never the
only signal.

  --success    settled · confirmed · done · succeeded    6.29:1 / 8.15:1
  --attention  now · next · warning · needs you          6.08:1 / 8.17:1  (ink)
  --danger     overdue · failed · invalid                6.10:1 / 6.06:1

`--info` is the interactive hue on purpose: an informational message
is the same "neutral, no action implied" register as a link.

`-ink` is the text-safe step; the bare token is for marks and fills.
`-surface` and `-line` are the wash and its edge: 12% / 32% of the hue
in light, 20% / 44% in dark.

io.brignano.note: 3.85:1 in light — mark/fill only, NOT text
6.08:1 / 8.17:1 — mark and label converge in dark

diff-added.$description:
── Diff ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
What a change did to a thing: a deploy, a plan, a pull request. Aliases
of the state hues, so a diff adds no hue of its own (DESIGN.md §9):

  --diff-added    created by this change      success — settled
  --diff-changed  modified by this change     interactive — informational
  --diff-removed  removed by this change      danger — can lose data

Always with a symbol and a word (+ added, ~ changed, − removed).

code-surface.$description:
── Code ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Syntax colour without a rainbow (DESIGN.md §3): keywords take the
interactive cobalt ink, everything else is a step of the neutral ramp,
and weight and italics do the rest. All aliases, so code adds no hue.

  --code-surface   the block, inset one step below the card
  --code-keyword   if, return, const — cobalt ink
  --code-string    literals — secondary ink
  --code-comment   comments — slate, set in italics
  --code-highlight a highlighted line — the cobalt wash

mark.$description:
── Mark — identity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
Inks a GRAPHIC: a product's glyph, the A|B monogram, a hero rule. That is
the entire permitted use.

It is NOT a button, chip, badge, wash, border, or link. If you are
reaching for it to tint a UI element, the answer is a neutral or a
state colour — see DESIGN.md §3.

It shares larch amber with --attention deliberately: the identity and
the attention state are the same warmth, and because --mark never
appears as a UI surface the two can never be mistaken for each other
in the same context.

io.brignano.note: when the mark carries a label, 6.08:1 / 8.17:1

mark-teal.$description:
── Product marks — one per product page ─────────────────────────────
Each product's marketing page picks one, so Driftwood, Guidebook and
Sites don't read as the same page with the words swapped (ADR-0011).
Same contract as --mark: it inks the product's graphics (its glyph,
the hero rule, the proof's stage, step numerals), never a link, text
or state. On a product page only, it may also fill the primary button
and wash the ground, through the -fill and -surface steps below
(ADR-0017). Hues sit away from cobalt (act), forest
(success), amber (attention) and rust (danger). All ≥ 3:1 on --bg and
--card in both themes. product-page.css maps one onto --pp-mark via
data-mark on .pp.

mark-fill.$description:
── A mark as a fill and a ground — product pages only (ADR-0017) ────
On a product's marketing page, and nowhere else, the mark may fill the
one primary button and wash the page ground. Never in an app, never a
link, text or a state. The mark tokens above don't move: like --action beside
--action-ink and --danger-fill beside --danger, the fill is its own step.

  -fill          the button, under a white --on-mark label in both themes.
                 In light it IS the mark (amber is deepened to carry the
                 label); in dark it sits at the mark's hue, as light as a
                 white label allows (4.5:1), the method ADR-0015 used
                 for cobalt.
  -fill-hover, -fill-pressed   step darker in both themes.
  -surface       the page ground: a faint, opaque tint at the mark's hue
                 that --ink, --ink-soft and --action-ink all read on.

Labels, light / dark:   fill          hover         pressed
  amber (the family)    4.60 / 4.61   6.09 / 5.65   7.63 / 6.92
  teal                  4.95 / 4.56   6.70 / 5.60   8.31 / 6.90
  violet                6.05 / 4.57   8.23 / 5.68   10.24 / 6.94
  magenta               5.79 / 4.57   7.83 / 5.61   9.71 / 6.91

Use the unprefixed four: `data-mark` points them at a product's, as it
does --mark-current. With no attribute they are the family amber.

mark-current.$description:
The mark in force here (ADR-0014): the family amber until `data-mark`
on an ancestor, usually <html>, names a product's. A brand glyph and
.rule draw in this, so a product's colour follows it from its marketing
page into its app and onto its error pages. The [data-mark] rules below
only point it at a token above; they declare no colour of their own.

forest.$description:
── Legacy aliases ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
Kept so existing `life` components keep compiling. Do not use in new
work — reach for the semantic tokens above.

--larch-deep is written out rather than aliased, because "deep"
inverts: darker in light, BRIGHTER in dark. An alias to either role
silently changes one theme — it moved .pill-active from #f0bd74 to
#e0a44f before this was caught.

action-edge.$description:
── Tokens the kits set (ADR-0019) ──
Each is an alias here, so today's look is unchanged; a kit in kits/*.css
gives it a value of its own.

The primary button's border. The fill carries itself, except in a kit
whose fill can't be found on its page (Split in light).

accent.$description: The one highlight a screen may carry, and its label.

data-mark-teal.$description:
── A product's mark, wherever the product is ──────────────────────────
One attribute per product: <html data-mark="teal">. Works on any element,
so a page that shows two products can mark each one's section. It also
points the product-page fill and ground (ADR-0017) at the product's.
